summary: Route metadata desync causes shadow fallbacks during canary cutover for tenant FluxHealth
description: Issue summary: During a staged canary cutover for FluxHealth's dedicated tenant, a subset of routed requests started returning responses from the shadow/legacy variant despite the tenant being explicitly model-pinned to redwood-xl-2.7B. Impact: Production traffic experienced mixed-model outputs for ~6% of sessions in us-east, resulting in degraded model quality for customer-facing features and repeated client-side retries. Environment: Dedicated cluster for FluxHealth spanning prod-us-east and prod-eu-west, canary weight applied to 20% of traffic in us-east. Timeline: 2026-03-10 09:02 UTC - canary rollout initiated from Console; 09:07 UTC - first anomalies reported by FluxHealth; 09:10 UTC - increased 5xxs and mixed responses observed; 09:24 UTC - initial triage by Support and SRE. Observed behavior: Requests that included explicit tenant pin metadata still routed to legacy shadow variant intermittently. Edge logs indicate fallback decisions were taken using an older route metadata snapshot that did not include the updated fallback_map and roll-forward policy. This appears correlated with the region-specific metadata propagation window during the canary slice update.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On a dedicated tenant with an active model pin (redwood-xl-2.7B), initiate a staged canary slice update that patches route metadata in the control plane (fallback_map change + new canary weight).
2) Simulate traffic from us-east with 20% sampling for the canary cohort and keep session affinity across multiple requests.
3) Observe routing decisions at the edge and check if any requests are routed to the legacy shadow variant despite pin header present.
4) Correlate timestamps with control-plane metadata snapshots and edge-cache TTLs to reproduce the desync window.
logs: 2026-03-10T09:07:12Z edge-proxy[ingress] INFO tenant=fluxhealth req_id=abc123 route_select=shadow_fallback reason=metadata_snapshot_mismatch snapshot_id=2026-03-09T23:50:10Z
2026-03-10T09:07:13Z orchestrator WARN tenant=fluxhealth apply_patch=canary-slice-45 status=partial success=true missing_keys=[fallback_map]
2026-03-10T09:09:01Z serving-runtime ERROR tenant=fluxhealth model_mismatch=expected(redwood-xl-2.7B) actual(legacy-shadow-1.3) latency=312ms
investigation_notes: Support triaged with SRE and confirmed deviation affects a small cohort in us-east where canary weight was applied.

Edge inspection shows edge cache used a snapshot timestamp older than the control-plane commit for the fallback_map key; metadata push succeeded in control-plane but TTL-based invalidation on edge didn't fire immediately.
Hypothesis 1: Control-plane metadata patch applied in phased manner (region-first), but edge cache invalidation was scoped incorrectly and left a stale fallback map in place for some shards.
Hypothesis 2: Patch ordering: canary weight update committed before fallback_map update in control-plane, creating a temporary state where routing logic falls back to legacy priority list.
Action taken: Forced a metadata sync to the edge for tenant fluxhealth at 09:31 UTC and flushed route metadata caches for affected shards.
Metric check: After cache flush, legacy-variant routing dropped to <0.1% within 3 minutes; client retries returned to expected model outputs.
resolution: Mitigation applied: manual metadata re-sync + shard cache flush for FluxHealth at 2026-03-10T09:31Z. Follow-up fix: control-plane patch ordering guard introduced in PR #4221 to ensure fallback_map is committed atomically with rollout weights; edge-proxy PR #1987 adds a robust metadata-change webhook to trigger immediate shard invalidation. Customer notified and monitoring remains active. Postmortem requested and scheduled (link above).
